items.title: Chick Corea — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: That was the workshop idea for me and Stanley this week, was some young musicians who are incredible to play with—Ravi Coltrane; Charles Altura, who is a real discovery for me on the guitar; and Marcus Gilmore, who is Roy Haynes’ grandson, who is just an amazing creative man...

ctx.x: Finally, you like to talk about the future, and you’ve talked about the future. But in the here and now, there’s another new band that you’ll be going on stage with in promptly two hours and twenty-five minutes.

Yes. There’s another new band that’s leading into another new band actually. Because that balance I was talking about of connecting with my old friends and doing collaborations, kind of went... It went this way, and I needed to bring it more this way in terms of me writing and putting my own ideas together with a new band. That was the workshop idea for me and Stanley this week, was some young musicians who are incredible to play with—Ravi Coltrane; Charles Altura, who is a real discovery for me on the guitar;…
And who has toured with you in the past.
